audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers are built around blinding Blooming Blows. Blooming Blows is an ability — Lillia activates it to deal magic damage in an area around herself, with extra true damage on the edge. Blinding Dart suppresses basic attacks and has no effect on it. The same error appears in the full layer's tldr, winCon, enemyWin, focus, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull and phases[1].why.
audit.why: Lillia's entire damage output is Q, W, E and R — all abilities. Blind is close to dead weight in this matchup, and telling a Teemo to hold Q for her trade means holding it forever. This is the reason the advice does not match a 53.18% win rate.
audit.corrected: Blind does not touch any of Lillia's damage. You beat her with 680 range, Move Quick spacing and shroom coverage, and you spend Q for its own damage rather than saving it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states the precondition on Lilting Lullaby: it only affects enemies who already have Dream Dust on them. spikes[1] presents it as an unconditional 'sleep through walls' execution tool.
audit.why: This is the single most actionable fact in the matchup and it inverts the advice. If Lillia has not landed a spell on you, her ultimate does nothing to you at all. The play is therefore to take zero chip while R is up — not to fear a wall-sleep you cannot avoid.
audit.corrected: Lilting Lullaby only drowses enemies carrying Dream Dust. Refuse her poke and her 150/130/110s ultimate has no target.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (R: 'causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy')

audit.whatIsWrong: Swirlseed (E) reveals stealth, and nothing in either layer mentions it.
audit.why: Guerrilla Warfare invisibility is Teemo's defining defensive and ambush tool, and Lillia is one of the few top laners who strips it at 700 range on a 12s cooldown. A Teemo sitting in brush expecting to be unseen is the exact mistake this matchup punishes. Swirlseed also keeps rolling until it hits a wall or a target, so its effective range from open ground is much longer than 700.
audit.corrected: Swirlseed reveals you in brush and out of Guerrilla Warfare invisibility, on a flat 12s cooldown, and it rolls until it hits terrain or a body.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (E Swirlseed, revealsStealth flag, range 700, cd 12)

audit.whatIsWrong: Ability names are shuffled throughout. 'her W Dream Dust', 'the outer ring of her W', 'her W (Lilting Lullaby does not apply yet, but her Dream Dust E)', 'bouncing Q ring'. W is Watch Out! Eep! (a zone with a heavy centre). The edge/ring with the true damage is Q. Dream Dust comes from the passive, Dream-Laden Bough. Lilting Lullaby is R.
audit.why: The 'mid' sentence in particular is not just misnamed, it is ungrammatical and unparseable. A reader cannot act on any of it.
audit.corrected: Q Blooming Blows = AoE with true damage on the edge. W Watch Out! Eep! = zone, heaviest in the centre. E Swirlseed = rolling projectile. R Lilting Lullaby = the sleep.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] says her Blooming Blows move speed 'is online at level one and she can already float'. The Q passive grants stacking move speed only when she hits enemies with spells.
audit.why: It is earned, not free. That gives Teemo a concrete denial play — every spell she misses is speed she does not have — which the current text hides.
audit.corrected: Her speed stacks come from landing spells. Dodge and she is a slow champion with no dash.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (Q: 'Passively, Lillia gains stacking Move Speed when hitting enemies with spells')

audit.whatIsWrong: 'late' claims 'your poison plus shroom damage crumbles towers faster than she can rotate'.
audit.why: Toxic Shot poison and Noxious Trap do not damage structures. The split-push argument is sound but the mechanism given for it is false, and a player who believes it will misjudge every tower timer.
audit.corrected: Attribute the tower pressure to Nashor's-boosted attack speed on the tower, not to poison or mushrooms.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (E Toxic Shot is an on-hit poison; R Noxious Trap is an enemy-triggered trap)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content level chart gives Lillia six of seven stages with 'Skill' at first item, and the prose says 'she WILL outscale your teamfight utility'. The full layer's chart gives Teemo four stages and Skill three, and the packet shows Teemo at 53.18% over 425 games. The two charts agree on zero stages.
audit.why: A Teemo reading this is told he loses a lane he actually wins, and the two charts on the same page contradict each other completely. The narrative was written for a losing matchup and the numbers say otherwise.
audit.corrected: Not auto-flipping the whole chart — that is a bigger call than an audit should make unilaterally. But the direction is wrong and the two layers need reconciling against the 53.18% figure. Flagging as the top structural item on this matchup.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer refers to Lillia as 'he' and 'his' throughout — tldr, winCon, breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, trading, dosFull.
audit.why: Lillia is female. It reads as machine-generated and undermines trust in everything else on the page.

edits.after: Blooming Blows only stacks her move speed when she LANDS a spell on you — dodge the first ones and she is a slow champion with no dash. Blind never touches it; it is an ability, not an auto.

edits.after: Lilting Lullaby only drowses targets already carrying Dream Dust — if she has not landed a spell on you, her 150/130/110s ultimate has nothing to grab. Refuse the chip.

edits.after: Refuse every scrap of chip damage while her ultimate is up — no Dream Dust on you means no sleep

edits.after: Stack Blooming Blows speed by landing spells and clip you with its edge, where the extra damage is true, from outside your poison range

edits.after: Blooming Blows only accelerates her once she lands spells on someone, so level 1 is the one time she is genuinely slow — punish it, because every hit she gets is speed she keeps.

edits.before: She now has her W Dream Dust — the bounce damage catches you if you step back, and her passive speed acceleration means she controls the trade distance your Q blind depends on.
edits.after: Watch Out! Eep! is a zone that hits hardest in the centre, and the edge of Blooming Blows adds true damage — two different abilities, and blind stops neither of them.

edits.before: With E and Q both live, her kite loop (ring outer, float back, let DOT tick) outpaces your poke; she takes almost no sustained damage because she never auto-commits.

edits.after: Lilting Lullaby is a 1600-range map-wide threat, but only against targets already carrying Dream Dust — take no chip while it is up and her 150/130/110s ultimate finds nothing.

edits.before: Lillia controls levels 1-3 because her Blooming Blows passive speed lets her float at exactly the distance where your E poison barely ticks and your Q blind is wasted on a target not autoing. Your job is not to win these trades — it is to deny her free stack-building. Stand at your wave, Q only when she commits a real Blooming Blows auto, and let the poison chip accumulate over many tiny windows rather than forcing a duel she kites freely. Doran's Shield and a magic-resist shard blunt her burst significantly; she is an off-meta pick with lower base stats than most lane bullies, so surviving early is already winning.
edits.after: Lillia's Blooming Blows move speed is earned, not free — it stacks only when she hits enemies with spells, so levels 1-3 are the window where she is a slow champion with no dash. Every spell you dodge is speed she never gets. Be clear-eyed about your Q: Blinding Dart does nothing to her damage, because Q, W, E and R are all abilities. Spend it for the damage, not as a saved counter. Stand at your wave, poison her on every step-up, and hold your 680 range against a champion whose Q only reaches 450. Doran's Shield and an MR shard blunt the chip meaningfully.

edits.before: At levels 4-5 Lillia's W (Lilting Lullaby does not apply yet, but her Dream Dust E) and bouncing Q ring let her chain trades you cannot answer melee — do not chase her into the jungle where her passive speed is amplified. Plant shrooms on the tribush and river bushes NOW to reclaim vision, and start using your own lane-center shrooms to zone her last-hits when she is low on HP. Level 6 is her biggest threat spike: a sleeping dart from her R through a jungle wall into a gank is a death sentence. The moment she hits 6, shroom both entry points and keep track of her position on the minimap before pushing up.
edits.after: At levels 4-5 her pattern is Swirlseed from 700 into Watch Out! Eep! and the Blooming Blows edge, where the extra damage is true — three abilities, none of them blindable. Do not chase her into the jungle, where her stacked speed compounds. Swirlseed also reveals stealth, so brush and Guerrilla Warfare are not cover against her. Level 6 is the spike, but read it correctly: Lilting Lullaby only drowses targets already carrying Dream Dust. Arrive at 6 clean and her ultimate has nothing to grab. Shroom both jungle entries and watch her minimap position before stepping up.

edits.before: Your win condition is the map, not the duel. Lillia is an off-meta top pick who transitions into a teamfight AOE-sleep bot — she WILL outscale your teamfight utility. Force the game to never reach that state: with Liandry's Angueur, a shroom-walled side lane is a 1v1 you deny entirely because she cannot walk into your mushroom field without taking lethal DOT stacks, and your poison plus shroom damage crumbles towers faster than she can rotate. If she leaves top to help her team, you take towers; if she stays, she is marooned in a side lane where her AOE teamfight R is irrelevant. Win by making the game unplayable for her in whichever direction she chooses.
edits.after: Your win condition is the map, not the duel. Lillia scales into an AoE sleep engine for teamfights, so force the game to resolve before that matters: with Liandry's, a shroom-walled side lane is a 1v1 she cannot enter without eating stacked DoT, and Nashor's attack speed is what actually takes the tower — mushrooms and poison do nothing to structures, so never plan a tower timer around them. If she leaves top to help her team, you take the tower; if she stays, she is marooned in a side lane where her AoE ultimate is worth nothing to her team. Make both directions lose for her, and never facecheck a bush she has Swirlseed up for.

notes: This is the weakest entry in my slice by a wide margin and I gave it the most work. Three independent problems compound: (a) the whole matchup is written around blinding Blooming Blows, which is an ability and cannot be blinded, so the headline advice in BOTH layers is inert; (b) the level chart says Lillia wins six of seven stages and the prose says she outscales you, while the packet says Teemo wins 53.18% over 425 games and the full layer's own chart gives Teemo four stages — the two charts agree on zero stages; (c) the full layer calls Lillia 'he' throughout. I fixed (a) and (c) in the strings I touched and reported (b) rather than flipping seven sides unilaterally, but (b) needs a human decision and this matchup should not ship until it is made. Champion-wide defects also apply: "Blinding Shot" x271 and "Liandry's Angueur" x80 in champ-data/content/teemo.js both need one global replace. Separately: the phrase 'percent-max-HP'/'percent-HP' appears 19 times across content/teemo.js and at least the K'Sante instances are fabricated (his kit has no percent-health component) — worth auditing all 19.
